newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE sees A$ averaging US$0.7800 in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE sees A$ averaging US$0.7800 in 1997/98.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) on Tuesday forecast the Australian dollar would average US$0.7800 in the fiscal year to June 1998.
The bureau also said low inflation and banking competition left room for further falls in Australian commercial interest rates, and it forecast slower economic growth than the Treasury.
Australian GDP in the fiscal year to June would be just 3.2 percent higher than in 1995/96, the bureau said.
The latest Treasury forecast for 1996/97 GDP growth is 3.5 percent.

Average consumer prices in 1996/97 were seen 2.3 percent higher than the previous year, excluding interest rate effects, compared with the Treasury's 2.0 percent forecast for "underlying inflation," which is slightly different.
The bureau prepares economic forecasts as forecasting assumptions for its commodities outlook.
"The Australian dollar is assumed to average around US$0.7800 in 1997/98 -- the same as in 1996/97," it said.
This reflected the moderate rises expected in Australian commodity prices in 1997/98.
"However, it is also expected that interest rate differentials between Australia and Australia's major trading partners will continue to narrow in the short term," the bureau added.
This would limit any upward pressure on the Australian dollar from the commodity prices.
"Given the outlook for continued low inflation and increased competition in the banking sector, there are prospects for further reductions in Australia's prime lending rates," the bureau said.
The Reserve Bank of Australia, which eased monetary policy three times between July and December 1996, said last month that current monetary settings were appropriate.
